aspects.says: ArrayList.removeAll and retainAll call contains on their argument for each element, so with a List argument they are O(n^2).
basis: section:A Call Inside a Loop Multiplies: List.contains in a Loop Is O(n²)

aspects.says: At small n the constant costs Big O drops can make the higher-order code faster, as insertion sort beat merge sort up to 512 elements on one machine; for a fixed small n Big O does not rank the choices.
basis: section:At Small n, Constants and the Cache Decide

aspects.says: List.contains scans, so calling it once per element of a loop is O(n^2); a HashSet built once before the loop keeps the loop O(n), and building it inside the loop is quadratic again.
basis: section:A Call Inside a Loop Multiplies: List.contains in a Loop Is O(n²)

aspects.says: The same call can make a different number of operations on a different input: List.sort makes n - 1 comparisons on sorted input and about n log n on shuffled input.
basis: section:Count the Operations: Doubling n Shows the Order
aspects.reason: a property of the JDK's sort that the page shows by counting; a practice would only re-run the JDK's sort, so nothing the reader writes would be graded

aspects.says: Counting the innermost operation at n and 2n gives the order: a ratio of 2 is linear, about 2.2 is n log n, 4 is quadratic; Big O keeps that growth and drops constant factors.
basis: section:Count the Operations: Doubling n Shows the Order

aspects.says: Amortised O(1) is an average: the add that grows an ArrayList copies every element, so a large list has rare, large pauses; presizing removes them.
basis: section:Amortised O(1): ArrayList.add Copies Each Element a Few Times, Not n Times

aspects.says: A growable array that grows its capacity in proportion to its size copies a small multiple of n elements over n adds, so add is amortised O(1); a fixed growth step makes the total O(n^2).
basis: section:Amortised O(1): ArrayList.add Copies Each Element a Few Times, Not n Times
